title: The disciples, closed
hook: the ones who walked with him, and who we are like

segments.voice: Yesterday, sangha: wise, powerful, slow, proud and gentle, all welcomed. Your line was all were welcome. Today, this part of the path closes.

Two friends at a festival who suddenly found the show empty. A cousin who remembered everything he heard. A strict elder in a patched robe. A barber ordained ahead of princes. A boy who had never heard the words there isn't. A queen and her mirror, a mother and her mustard seed, a merchant and a grove covered in gold, a sweeper among thrown-away flowers. For weeks now the path has walked beside the people who walked beside the Buddha. Today it leaves one question with you.
screen: `A FESTIVAL, A BARBER, A BOY.` → `A QUEEN, A MOTHER, A SWEEPER.` → `ONE QUESTION.`

segments.voice: First, the friends. Sariputta and Moggallana made a pact that whoever found the deathless first would tell the other, and kept it. Wisdom and power, side by side. Second, the rememberers. Ananda kept the door and the words. Upali kept the rules. Kassapa kept the strict practices and called the council so the teaching wouldn't be lost. Anuruddha, the boy who never heard there isn't, learned what the work of the fields costs. Third, the women and the lay followers. Mahapajapati went first. Khema, Patacara, Dhammadinna and Kisa Gotami taught and were taught. Visakha and Anathapindika gave, and Citta, a householder, taught monks. Fourth, the warnings and the welcome. Slow Culapanthaka and the sweeper Sunita were let in. Proud Channa was met with silence and came back. Devadatta split the sangha, and even he has a far door left open in the texts. The Anguttara Nikaya has a chapter naming the foremost, and each is foremost in something different: one in wisdom, one in power, one in learning, one in the discipline, a nun in teaching, a layman in giving. It's a gallery, not a ladder. And when the Buddha was dying, he named no one to take his place. In the Mahaparinibbana Sutta he tells Ananda that the teaching and the discipline will be their teacher. So the disciples aren't a line of successors. They're a set of mirrors.
screen: `THE FRIENDS: WISDOM AND POWER.` · `THE ONES WHO REMEMBERED.` · `THE WOMEN AND THE LAY FOLLOWERS.` · `THE WARNINGS AND THE WELCOME.` · then, large: `WHICH ONE ARE YOU?`

segments.voice: Let the faces pass by slowly: the friend who ran to share good news, the attendant who held the door, the one who couldn't remember a verse, the proud one, the grieving mother, the generous merchant. One will stay a little longer than the others; don't choose the one you'd like to be, choose the one you are this season, flaws included. Sit with them for a while, as company.
The disciples. The people who walked with the Buddha: wise, slow, proud, grieving, generous, and each remembered by name. Today's word.
Your line: which one are you. Somewhere among them is a face that looks a little like yours. Day seven hundred eighty, done.

howItsDone: Buddhist teachers retell the great disciples' stories in talks and festivals, and in Theravada countries the chief disciples Sariputta and Moggallana are honored together, with images of them standing on either side of the Buddha.

chat.says: Who took over leading the community after the Buddha died?
options: He named no one; the teaching and the discipline would be their teacher.
Devadatta, once the Buddha agreed to hand the whole order to him.
Sariputta, the wisest disciple, who outlived him and took charge.
chat.meaning: In the Mahaparinibbana Sutta the dying Buddha names no successor. He tells Ananda the teaching and the discipline will be their teacher.

Anguttara Nikaya.meaning: a Pali collection; one chapter names each disciple's strength

Mahaparinibbana Sutta.meaning: the discourse on the Buddha's last days

Upali.meaning: the former barber who kept the rules

Anuruddha.meaning: the boy who had never heard 'there isn't'

Mahapajapati.meaning: the Buddha's foster mother, the first nun

notes: Closing day of Block B (725–780); the hook and teach summarize earlier days (725–779). Check each summary against those days' scripts, especially days not yet written when this was drafted.

Etadagga examples as paraphrased: Sariputta wisdom, Moggallana psychic power, Ananda learning, Upali discipline, Dhammadinna foremost among nuns in teaching dhamma, Anathapindika foremost among lay donors. Confirm.
Citta is named in AN 1 as foremost among laymen who teach dhamma; the script says only that he taught monks (day 770).
